sentence: This project builds computer-based methods that protect genomic data so untrusted people analyzing it cannot see an individual's personal genetic information.
This project studies why people with obesity and diabetes face a higher risk of severe infection, looking at vaccination, antibodies and human immune organoids.
This project builds deep learning methods that use a wearable device for infants to detect sleep and wake states, physical activity and household noise.
This project builds a chemical footprinting method to study how biomolecular condensation changes in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia.
This project studies whether high temperature and poor air quality raise the risk of heart and lung problems in breast cancer survivors after cancer therapy.
This project offers stem cells, organoids and genome editing services to help investigators study how digestive diseases work.
This project tries to find out how a fusion protein drives acute megakaryoblastic leukemia, a pediatric cancer.
This project studies affective visual processing soon after trauma to find brain mechanisms that lead to posttraumatic stress disorder.
This project builds deep learning methods that use clinical knowledge to predict and understand suicide from longitudinal data.
This project builds imaging tools and machine learning to predict drug efficacy and toxicity in 3D cell culture models.
This project studies how amino acid metabolism helps glioblastoma cells grow and resist current therapies.
This project studies how telomere dysfunction leads to lung disease, including idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
This project studies how airway lining cells use a signaling pathway called Notch to control airway white blood cells in asthma, using mouse models.
This project studies how lymphocytes move from the blood into organs such as the lungs, stomach and pancreas.
This project studies how a family of RNA binding proteins recognizes and chemically changes RNA in cells and how this affects neurons.
This project builds a way to do breast MRI with the patient lying on her back to give sharper images.
This project tests whether radiotherapy plus a second treatment can help breast cancer overcome resistance to immune checkpoint inhibition.
This project tests whether combining radiation with the drug olaparib makes pancreatic cancers respond to immunotherapy.
This project holds a workshop where scientists discuss advances in musculoskeletal biology related to bone disease.
This project tests the thinking of young adult cancer survivors in real time during daily life to find risk factors for long-term cognitive impairment.
